page: Amazon Web Services c7gd.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by custom AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processors utilizing the ARM64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs running at 2.6 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and is bundled with 118 GB of local NVMe SSD instance store storage. Network performance is rated at a 1 Gbps baseline.

Benchmark data shows average single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores landing in the middle 50% tier. However, multi-core and multi-threaded workloads show limitations, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core results categorized as weak. Memory bandwidth is mixed, showing average performance for large block read-only operations at 53.57 GB/sec, but weak performance for write operations and small block reads. Cryptographic and complex vector operations are limited, as indicated by poor Passmark CPU encryption and extended instruction scores.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c7gd.large offers a resource-dense profile by combining dedicated ARM64 cores with high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. This makes it suitable for single-threaded tasks, lightweight web serving, and local-storage-dependent workloads that do not require massive multi-threaded compute or large memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include basic database operations, single-threaded file compression, and lightweight application hosting.
